patients.label: 14-year-old girl with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes treated with metformin then empagliflozin

identity_evidence.quote: a case of empagliflozin use in a 14-year-old girl with poorly controlled T2D

attribution_limitations: The text says the patient was 14 years old when she presented to the center (the first visit), while Table 1 lists age 13.3 years at the 1st visit (20/03/2023); same timepoint, values differ (Table 1 lists 14 at the 2nd visit).

The text gives TIR 61% when empagliflozin was started (baseline of 'TIR increased from 61% to 91%'), whereas Table 1 lists TIR 62% at the 3rd visit labelled START empagliflozin; both describe the empagliflozin-initiation timepoint, so both are quarantined as source_conflict.

After six months of empagliflozin the text reports HbA1c 6.2% and TIR 91%, while Table 1 lists HbA1c 6.4% and TIR 91% at the 4th visit (14/06/2024), about four months after the 3rd visit, and HbA1c 6.5% at the last visit.

The text says metformin therapy was increased to 2 g per day and weight and HbA1c were assessed after 12 months, while Table 1 lists metformin 1500 mg/d at the 2nd visit and 2000 mg/d at the 3rd visit.
Table 1 prints units for the renal function row as mg/dl for both creatinine and ACR, and spells empagliflozin "Empaglifozin".

She was born full term after a pregnancy complicated by gestational diabetes; maternal grandparents had T2D and her mother had thyroid cancer.

claims.text: At her first visit she was in good general condition with obesity (BMI 30 kg/m²) and acanthosis nigricans on the neck and armpits, on multiple daily insulin (glargine 9 U, lispro 12 U) with HbA1c 8.5%. Insulin was reduced and metformin started, then insulin was gradually stopped and metformin increased to 2 g per day with a hypocaloric diet, dietitian consultations and 10 hours per week of physical activity; after 12 months weight fell by 10 kg (BMI 30 to 26.4 kg/m²) and HbA1c was 7.4%.

claims.text: One year later glycemic control remained suboptimal (TIR 61% in the text, 62% in Table 1), so empagliflozin 10 mg daily was started with metformin for persistent hyperglycemia. After six months HbA1c decreased from 7.4% to 6.2% and TIR rose to 91%, with a stable weight of 75 kg and BMI 26.2 kg/m². No adverse events such as diabetic ketoacidosis or genital infections were reported, renal function was normal, and blood pressure did not change meaningfully; Table 1 follow-up continues to the last visit.
